chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
that he disliked the eating of every creature possessing a sting.

key_terms.ذِي حُمَةٍ: one possessing a sting — encompasses scorpions, bees, wasps, hornets, and any venomous stinging creature
key_terms.كَرِهَ: disliked / deemed reprehensible (karaha) — a term indicating something between outright prohibition and permissibility in Islamic jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat scorpions and stinging insects according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) expressed a religious dislike (karaha) for consuming any creature that possesses a sting — such as scorpions, bees, wasps, and other venomous insects. This ruling appears in Al-Kafi's chapter on animals whose flesh is prohibited or discouraged, establishing a comprehensive principle covering all stinging creatures. The use of 'karaha' (dislike) rather than 'tahrim' (prohibition) indicates this is classified as reprehensible (makruh) in Shia jurisprudence, though many jurists treat such creatures as forbidden due to the universal harm principle.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Gayas Bin Ibrahim,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having disliked eating all those with a sting (scorpion etc.)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
disliked using poisonous things for food.’”
